bounded_statement: Within the supplied files for case:8b55946a92793ebcd387, the selected result (a pooled two-sample Student t-test reporting t(38) = 8.691, p < 1e-08 over 40 blade records) treats each of the 40 blade rows as an independent observation, even though the data description designates growline_id as the independent unit and each of the 8 growlines contributes exactly 5 blade rows. Each authorized independent unit (growline) therefore enters the row-independent procedure (scipy.stats.ttest_ind) five times, inflating the effective sample size from 8 growlines to 40 blades and the degrees of freedom from 6 to 38. A growline-level test on the 8 per-growline means (sparse: 2.10, 2.30, 2.00, 2.60; dense: 1.70, 1.50, 1.90, 1.30) yields approximately t(6) ≈ 3.5, p ≈ 0.013, so the direction of the effect survives but the reported statistical strength (p < 1e-08) is not supported at the correct unit of analysis.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report transparently discloses the unit structure (8 growlines, 5 blade records per growline) and lists per-growline means, showing the authors were aware of the clustering; however, these per-growline summaries are descriptive only and are never used in the inferential test, so this does not negate the issue.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: Per-growline means reported descriptively; inference still at blade level

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the finding in three ways. First, I searched workflow/analysis.py for any aggregation to the growline level before the significance test; the by_unit dictionary does compute per-growline values, but they are used only to print descriptive lines in the report, and stats.ttest_ind receives the raw per-blade arrays from by_group, so no unit-level inference exists. Second, I checked whether treatment might vary within a growline (which would make blades closer to legitimate experimental units); the data description and every CSV row confirm seeding_density is fixed for an entire growline. Third, I checked whether the report qualifies its claim (for example by flagging clustering or reporting a unit-level sensitivity analysis); the Method, Result, and selected-result sections present the blade-level t(38) test without any caveat. I also verified the arithmetic: 8 growlines x 5 blades = 40 rows, group n = 20 each, dof = 38, matching the report, and confirmed that a growline-level reanalysis gives a much weaker (though still significant) result, demonstrating the reported p-value materially depends on the repeated unit entries. All falsification attempts failed, so the issue stands as demonstrated.

root_cause: In workflow/analysis.py, main() appends every blade row's elongation value directly into by_group[seeding_density] and passes these per-blade arrays (n = 20 per group) to stats.ttest_ind with equal_var=True. The per-growline aggregation in by_unit is computed but used only for descriptive display in the report, not for inference. Because seeding density is assigned per growline and blades on one growline share rope, depth, and water column, the five blades per growline are repeated entries of the same independent unit into a procedure that assumes each row is independent, producing pseudoreplicated degrees of freedom (38 instead of 6) and a drastically overstated p-value.
